QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_9

question.text: A clearing member has total margin requirement of Rs. 50 lakhs. What is the minimum amount that must be in cash / cash equivalents?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires at least 50% of total collateral to be in cash / cash equivalents. 50% of Rs. 50 lakhs = Rs. 25 lakhs minimum in the cash component. The Trap: Rs. 50 lakhs assumes 100% must be cash; Rs. 10 lakhs implies 20%; Rs. 37.5 lakhs implies 75%. The mandated floor is 50%, not higher or lower. Note: Pages 257-258 and 268 confirm the 50% cash-equivalent rule at CM level. The workbook classifies FDRs, bank guarantees, Government securities, money market mutual fund units, gilt funds and sovereign gold bonds as cash component / cash equivalents (subject to haircut), while approved demat securities and certain other mutual fund units are treated as non-cash collateral subject to limits.
